observation.visible_scene: A dark speckled non-stick frying pan sits on a white portable induction/electric stove on a wooden tabletop. A hand grips the pan's black handle at the right edge to hold it steady. A second hand (fingers occasionally visible at the top edge) wields a yellow silicone spatula, which is in contact with two pale-yellow pats of butter inside the pan. Faint swirl marks of melted fat are visible on the pan surface.
visible_changes: Throughout the excerpt the spatula repeatedly pushes and slides the two butter pats across the pan floor, moving them between the left, center, and right areas of the cooking surface.
The butter pieces remain mostly solid block-like chunks, translating and occasionally being nudged together or split, rather than visibly dissolving within the segment.

The relative positions of the two pats change frame to frame: sometimes one is near the spatula edge and the other is set apart, sometimes they are close together, and at moments one is hidden behind the spatula head.
Melted-fat swirl patterns on the pan surface grow and shift as the spatula drags the butter around.
The pan, stove, and background stay fixed in frame, indicating the motion is object motion (spatula and butter), not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the butter eventually melts fully or is used as a base for further cooking.
The heat setting and what, if anything, is added after this segment.
The exact moment the spatula first entered the pan (motion is already underway at frame 1).
uncertain_details: Motion blur on the spatula and butter makes it hard to confirm whether a piece is occluded, merged, or actually missing in some frames (e.g., around frames 9 and 34).
The precise number of distinct butter chunks is ambiguous when the spatula head overlaps one of them.
It is unclear whether the spatula is spreading the butter to melt it or simply moving solid pieces around; only the sliding motion is directly visible.
